<details>
This is a systemd unit file that runs the llama-server binary from the llama.cpp project. It contains no malicious behavior: no network downloads, no obfuscated commands, no data exfiltration, and no unexpected file operations.

The file is actually an example of well-hardened packaging. The `%PKGVER%` placeholder in the Documentation URL is a normal packaging template substitution and poses no risk.

No injected code, no unexpected network hosts, no bypass of the declared source, and no deviation from standard packaging practice for a GPU-accelerated service.

<details>
The provided file is a systemd service unit (`llama-server-system.service`) for the LLaMA.cpp HTTP server, which is part of the `llama-prism-cuda-git` AUR package. It defines a well-structured, security-hardened service configuration with numerous protective measures typical of modern, secure service design.

The service uses `DynamicUser=yes`, runs under a dedicated unprivileged user/group, and employs extensive sandboxing: `ProtectSystem=strict`, `ProtectHome=yes`, `PrivateTmp=yes`, `PrivateIPC=yes`, `PrivateUsers=self`, and `PrivateMounts=yes` limit access to the host system. System call filtering (`SystemCallFilter=@system-service` and `~@privileged`) restricts kernel access, while `NoNewPrivileges=yes` prevents privilege escalation. Device access is explicitly whitelisted for GPU support (AMD, NVIDIA CUDA, HIP), which is expected for a GPU-accelerated LLM inference server. Environment variables are set to use service-private directories, and optional configuration can be loaded securely via `EnvironmentFile`.

All settings align with the intended functionality of exposing GPU resources to a local inference server while minimizing attack surface. There are no network download commands, no code execution from remote sources, no data exfiltration mechanisms, and no obfuscated logic. The file contains only declarative systemd configuration, which is inherently static and non-executable in the malicious sense. No evidence of supply-chain tampering or backdoor behavior is present.
</details>
